zajjaj:58-58.t:
﴿وَمِنهم مَن يَلْمِزُكَ في الصَّدَقاتِ﴾ (And among them is he who criticizes you concerning the charities), and it is also read ”يَلْمِزُونَكَ“. One says ”لَمَزْتُ الرَّجُلَ، ألْمِزُهُ“ — with kasra on the mīm — and ”ألْمُزُهُ“ — with ḍamma on the mīm — when you find fault with him; likewise ”هَمَزْتُهُ، أهْمِزُهُ“ when you find fault with him. The poet said:
؎إذا لَقِيتُكَ تُبْدِي لِي مُكاشَرَةً ∗∗∗ وإنْ تَغَيَّبْتُ كُنْتَ الهامِزَ اللُّمَزَةْ
(When I meet you, you show me a broad grin; and when I am absent, you are the backbiter, the fault-finder.)
”اَللُّمَزَةُ“ is one who finds much fault with people. Some said: ”اَللُّمَزَةُ“ is ”اَلْعَيِبُ“, with kasra on the ʿayn — i.e. with kasra on its ʿayn (middle radical) — ”عَيِبٌ“, like ”نَهِمٌ“, when he finds fault; what is meant by it is one who finds fault with his companion. And they said: ”اَللُّمْزَةُ“ is finding fault by whispering. All of this goes back to ”اَلْعَيْبُ“ (fault-finding).

zajjaj:60-60.t: And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿إنَّما الصَّدَقاتُ لِلْفُقَراءِ والمَساكِينِ والعامِلِينَ عَلَيْها والمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ (Charities are only for the poor, the needy, those employed to collect them, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled): these were people who used to be given [a share], their hearts being won over so that they would accept Islam; this is not in use today because Islam has prevailed. ﴿وَفِي الرِّقابِ﴾ (and for [freeing] necks): as when one assists the slave who has a contract of manumission (mukātab) until he frees his neck. ﴿والغارِمِينَ﴾ (and the debtors): they are those on whom debt has become binding through al-ḥimāla (standing surety); ”اَلْحِمالَةُ“ is giving [an undertaking] upon one's liability. It may also be that al-ghārim is one on whom a debt has become binding in something other than disobedience; and the more fitting view is that the debt paid off on his behalf be in something other than disobedience, because if the debt of one [incurred] in disobedience were paid off for him, that would be a strengthening [of him] in acts of disobedience. ﴿وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ (and in the way of Allah): i.e. and those who fight in jihad have a right in the charity. ﴿وابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ (and the son of the road): the son of the way; its interpretation is: one whose road has been cut off. ﴿فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ (an obligation from Allah) is accusative (manṣūb) as emphasis (tawkīd), because His saying “Charities are only for these” is like your saying “Allah has made the charities obligatory for these.” We have explained at the beginning of “al-Anfāl” what was said about all kinds of property, and treated it exhaustively. ”فَرِيضَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ“ (nominative) is also permissible on that basis, but I do not know that it has been read so.

zajjaj:61-61.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَمِنهُمُ الَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ النَّبِيَّ ويَقُولُونَ هو أُذُنٌ قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ﴾ (And among them are those who hurt the Prophet and say, “He is an ear.” Say: “An ear of good for you”). The explanation of the verse is that among the hypocrites was one who used to find fault with the Prophet ﷺ and say: “If [what I said] reaches him from me, I will swear to him and he will accept it from me, because he is an ear.” So Allah the Exalted made known that he is an ear of good for you, i.e. a listener to good for you. Then He made clear from whom he accepts, saying: ﴿يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ ويُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (he believes in Allah and believes the believers), i.e. he is an ear of good, not an ear of evil; he hears what Allah sends down to him and affirms it as true, and he believes the believers in what they inform him of. ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ﴾ (and a mercy to those of you who believe): i.e. he is a mercy, because he was the cause of the believers in their faith. Whoever reads ”أُذُنٌ خَيْرٌ لَكم“, the meaning is: one who listens to you and is close to you, accepting excuses, is better for you. It is related concerning this verse that a man among the hypocrites said: “If what Muḥammad has brought is true, then we are donkeys.” His wife's son said to him: “What he has brought is indeed true, and you are worse than this mount of yours.” That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and one of those present with him said: “We will apologize to him and swear to him, for he is an ear.”
And His saying: ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ لَكم لِيُرْضُوكُمْ﴾ (They swear by Allah to you to please you) [al-Tawba: 62]. One of the grammarians said that this lām has the sense of the oath, i.e. “they swear by Allah to you: they will surely please you (لَيُرْضُنَّكُمْ)”. This is a mistake, because they only swore that they had not said what was reported of them, in order to please you by the oath; they did not swear that they would please [you] in what lies ahead. ﴿واللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ أحَقُّ أنْ يُرْضُوهُ﴾ (But Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him) [al-Tawba: 62].
And His saying: ﴿إنْ كانُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (if they are believers) [al-Tawba: 62], i.e. if they are as they outwardly show, then they ought not to find fault with the Prophet ﷺ, and so by their allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ and abandoning faulting him they would be believers. In His saying ”وَرَحْمةٌ“ the genitive (jarr) is permissible by conjunction onto ”خَيْرٍ“, so the meaning would be: “Say: an ear of good for you and an ear of mercy for the believers.”
And His saying: ﴿أحَقُّ أنْ يُرْضُوهُ﴾ (have more right that they should please Him) [al-Tawba: 62] — He did not say ”يُرْضُوهُما“ (please them both), because the meaning indicates it, so He omitted it for lightness. The meaning is: “Allah has more right that they should please Him, and His Messenger has more right that they should please him,” as the poet said:
؎نَحْنُ بِما عِنْدَنا وأنْتَ بِما ∗∗∗ عِنْدَكَ راضٍ والأمْرَ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content — though the matter differs.)
The meaning is: “We are content (راضُونَ) with what we have, and you are content (راضٍ) with what you have.”

zajjaj:63-63.t: And His saying: ﴿ألَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أنَّهُ مَن يُحادِدِ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ﴾ (Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger): its meaning is “whoever is hostile to Allah and His Messenger, and whoever sets himself against Allah and His Messenger.” Its derivation in the language is like your saying “whoever keeps to a side apart from Allah and His Messenger,” i.e. “whoever is on one border (ḥadd) while Allah and His Messenger are on another border.” ﴿فَأنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ (then for him is the fire of Hell): the reading is with fatḥa and with kasra: ”فَإنَّ لَهُ“. Whoever reads it with kasra does so as a fresh start (istiʾnāf) after the fāʾ, as you say “then for him is the fire of Hell,” with ”إنَّ“ entering as an emphasizer. Whoever said ”فَأنَّ لَهُ“ only repeated ”فَأنَّ“ for emphasis, because when the speech became long, repeating it was more emphatic.

zajjaj:64-64.t: And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿يَحْذَرُ المُنافِقُونَ أنْ تُنَـزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (The hypocrites fear lest a sura be sent down about them). The wording of ”يَحْذَرُ“ is the wording of a statement (khabar), while its meaning is a command, because there is no ambiguity in the speech that it is a command; so it is like your saying “let the hypocrites beware (لِيَحْذَرِ المُنافِقُونَ)”. On this basis it is permissible, in anything that is commanded, for you to say ”يُفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ“ (that is done), standing in place of your saying ”لِيُفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ“ (let that be done). It may also be a statement about them, because they used to disbelieve out of obstinacy and envy; and the proof of this view is: ﴿قُلِ اسْتَهْزِئُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْرِجٌ ما تَحْذَرُونَ﴾ (Say: “Mock on! Allah will bring out what you fear.”)

zajjaj:65-65.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَئِنْ سَألْتَهم لَيَقُولُنَّ إنَّما كُنّا نَخُوضُ ونَلْعَبُ﴾ (And if you ask them, they will surely say, “We were only chatting idly and playing”): that is because they said: “We were only chatting idly as the riders [of a caravan] chat idly.”

zajjaj:66-66.t:
And His saying: ﴿لا تَعْتَذِرُوا قَدْ كَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إيمانِكُمْ﴾ (Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your faith): its interpretation is that your disbelief has become manifest after your displaying faith. ﴿إنْ نَعْفُ عَنْ طائِفَةٍ مِنكم نُعَذِّبْ طائِفَةً﴾ (If We pardon a party of you, We will punish a party). The reading is ”إنْ نَعْفُ“; and ”إنْ يُعْفَ“ and ”إنْ يَعْفُ“ are good, but I do not know anyone among the well-known [readers] who read them. It is related that these two parties were only three persons: two mocked and one laughed, so ”طائِفَةٌ“ was used for the single one. Likewise they said concerning His saying: ﴿وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذابَهُما طائِفَةٌ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (and let a party of the believers witness their punishment) [al-Nūr: 2], that what is meant by it is a single person, a ṭāʾifa.
And ”اَلطّائِفَةُ“ in the language has as its origin ”اَلْجَماعَةُ“ (the group), because it is the amount that goes around (يَطِيفُ) a thing; and it may be said of a single person ”طائِفَةٌ“, meaning by it one person who is a ṭāʾifa.

zajjaj:67-67.t:
And His saying: ﴿المُنافِقُونَ والمُنافِقاتُ بَعْضُهم مِن بَعْضٍ﴾ (The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are of one another): this follows His saying — Exalted is He —: ﴿وَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إنَّهم لَمِنكُمْ﴾ (And they swear by Allah that they are of you) [al-Tawba: 56], i.e. the hypocrites are not of the believers, because the hypocrites ﴿يَأْمُرُونَ بِالمُنْكَرِ﴾ (enjoin what is wrong), i.e. they enjoin disbelief in the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ المَعْرُوفِ﴾ (and forbid what is right), i.e. they forbid belief in him; ﴿وَيَقْبِضُونَ أيْدِيَهُمْ﴾ (and they close their hands), i.e. they do not give charity and do not pay zakat; ﴿نَسُوا اللَّهَ فَنَسِيَهُمْ﴾ (they forgot Allah, so He forgot them), i.e. they abandoned the command of Allah, so Allah abandoned them [and withheld from them] His mercy and His granting of success.
And His saying: ﴿هِيَ حَسْبُهُمْ﴾ (it is sufficient for them) [al-Tawba: 68], i.e. the sufficiency [matching] their sins, as you say: “I punished you according to (حَسَبَ) your deed,” and “What befell so-and-so is his ḥasb,” i.e. that is in proportion to his deed.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
And His saying: ﴿كالَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ (like those before you): the position of the kāf is accusative, i.e. Allah has threatened them [with punishment] for disbelieving in Him, as He threatened those before them.
And His saying: ﴿فاسْتَمْتَعُوا بِخَلاقِهِمْ﴾ (and they enjoyed their portion): it was said: they enjoyed their share of this world; and it was said: they enjoyed their religion. ”اَلْخَلاقُ“ is the portion which, in the eyes of its owner, is an ample share.

zajjaj:70-70.t: ﴿ألَمْ يَأْتِهِمْ نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وعادٍ﴾ (Has there not come to them the news of those before them, the people of Noah and ʿĀd): has there not come to them the report of those who perished in this world because of their sins, so that they might take heed? ”اَلْمُؤْتَفِكاتُ“ is the plural of ”مُؤْتَفِكَةٌ“: the earth was overturned (اِئْتَفَكَتْ) with them, i.e. turned upside down. It is said that they are the people of Lot, and it is said that they are all who were destroyed, as you say of one who perishes: “The world has turned over upon him.” ﴿فَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهم ولَكِنْ كانُوا أنْفُسَهم يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ (And Allah would not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves): Allah — exalted be His praise — made known that His punishing them was by their deserving it, and that this is justice.

zajjaj:72-72.t: And His saying: ﴿وَرِضْوانٌ﴾ (and good pleasure): it is read ”وَرُضْوانٌ“ and ”وَرِضْوانٌ“, and both of them are [transmitted] from ʿĀṣim. The meaning of ”وَرِضْوانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أكْبَرُ“ (and good pleasure from Allah is greater) is: greater than the bliss they are in.

zajjaj:73-73.t: And His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ جاهِدِ الكُفّارَ والمُنافِقِينَ﴾ (O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites): He commanded striving against them, and the meaning is: strive against them with fighting and with argument; so [establishing] the argument against the hypocrites is a striving against them.

zajjaj:74-74.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَهَمُّوا بِما لَمْ يَنالُوا﴾ (and they intended what they did not attain): it was said that they had intended to kill the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that they were twelve men who resolved to lie in wait for him at a mountain pass (ʿaqaba) on his route and assassinate him. Allah made that known to him, and when he reached them, he ordered that they be moved away from his path and named them man by man. This is among the greatest of his signs, because the matter in their story was known only through revelation. ﴿وَما نَقَمُوا إلا أنْ أغْناهُمُ اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ (And they resented nothing except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty): it was said “Allah and His Messenger enriched them” only because their wealth had increased from the spoils, and the cause of that was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
And His saying: ﴿يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ عَذابًا ألِيمًا في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ﴾ (Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter): its meaning is "causing pain" (مُؤْلِمًا). He said “in this world” only because it was commanded that they be killed. ”وَما نَقِمُوا“ (with kasra on the qāf) is also permissible.
[Translator's note: the Arabic reads «فَلَمّا بَلَغَ إلَيْهِمْ أمْرُ مَن نَحّاهم عَنْ طَرِيقِهِ», which is grammatically awkward; it is rendered here by its evident sense, “he ordered that they be moved away from his path.”]

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿وَمِنهم مَن عاهَدَ اللَّهَ لَئِنْ آتانا مِن فَضْلِهِ لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ﴾ (And among them is he who made a covenant with Allah: “If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity”): the original form is ”لَنَتَصَدَّقَنَّ“, but the tāʾ was assimilated (idghām) into the ṣād because of its closeness to it.

zajjaj:77-77.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَأعْقَبَهم نِفاقًا في قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ (So He made hypocrisy follow in their hearts): it may be that [since] ﴿فَلَمّا آتاهم مِن فَضْلِهِ بَخِلُوا بِهِ﴾ (But when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it) [al-Tawba: 76], He said: “So He made hypocrisy follow them,” i.e. Allah led them astray because of their deed.
[Translator's note: the sentence in the source appears incomplete («يَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ ﴿فَلَمّا آتاهم…﴾ قالَ: فَأعْقَبَهم»); it is translated as it stands, with "[since]" supplied.]

zajjaj:79-79.t: And His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ المُطَّوِّعِينَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (Those who criticize the believers who give voluntarily): ”يَلْمِزُونَ“ and ”يَلْمُزُونَ“, with kasra on the mīm and with ḍamma; its meaning is: they find fault. They had found fault with the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over charities they brought to the Prophet ﷺ. It is related that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān brought a purse that filled the palm, and that a man who was called Abū ʿAqīl brought a ṣāʿ of dates, so they found fault with him for that and said: “Muḥammad has no need of this man's ṣāʿ; he only brought this to have himself mentioned.” That is the meaning of ﴿والَّذِينَ لا يَجِدُونَ إلا جُهْدَهُمْ﴾ (and those who find nothing but their effort) — also ”جَهْدَهم“, with fatḥa and with ḍamma. ﴿فَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنهم سَخِرَ اللَّهُ مِنهُمْ﴾ (and they ridicule them — Allah ridicules them): ”اَلسِّخْرِيَّ“ from Allah is the requital of their deed, and we have explained that.

zajjaj:80-80.t: And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿إنْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهم سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ﴾ (If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them): it is related that the Prophet ﷺ said: “I will ask forgiveness for them more than seventy times,” and then there was revealed: ﴿سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهم أمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهم لَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ﴾ (It is all the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them) [al-Munāfiqūn: 6].

zajjaj:81-81.t: And His saying: ﴿فَرِحَ المُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلافَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ﴾ (Those who were left behind rejoiced in their staying behind, in opposition to the Messenger of Allah): [خِلافَ] in the sense of opposing the Messenger of Allah; it is accusative because it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: [they rejoiced] in that they stayed behind in order to oppose the Messenger of Allah. It is also read ”خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ“ (behind the Messenger of Allah), and here [the meaning] would be that they lagged behind from striving in the way of Allah. ﴿وَقالُوا لا تَنْفِرُوا في الحَرِّ قُلْ نارُ جَهَنَّمَ أشَدُّ حَرًّا﴾ (And they said, “Do not go forth in the heat.” Say: “The fire of Hell is more intense in heat”): this is a threat concerning abandoning striving. ”لا تَنْفُرُوا“, with ḍamma on the fāʾ, is also permissible.

zajjaj:82-82.t: ﴿فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلا ولْيَبْكُوا كَثِيرًا جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ (So let them laugh a little and weep much, as a recompense for what they used to earn): ”جَزاءً“ is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: “and let them weep as a recompense for this deed.”

zajjaj:84-84.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلا تُصَلِّ عَلى أحَدٍ مِنهم ماتَ أبَدًا ولا تَقُمْ عَلى قَبْرِهِ﴾ (And do not ever pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave): it is related that it was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, who was the head of the hypocrites. When death came to him, he sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him for one of his two garments to be shrouded in, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him one of them. Then the hypocrite sent [word] to the Messenger of Allah: “I want the one of your garments that was next to your skin,” so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent that to him. It was said to him about it: “Why did you send him your shirt to be shrouded in when he is a disbeliever?” He said: “My shirt will not avail him anything against Allah, but I hope from Allah that many people will enter Islam by this means.” It is related that a thousand of the Khazraj accepted Islam when they saw him seeking healing through the garment of the Messenger of Allah. He [the Prophet] wanted to pray over him, and the revelation came down upon him ﷺ: ﴿وَلا تُصَلِّ عَلى أحَدٍ مِنهُمْ﴾ (And do not pray over any of them). It is [also] related that he ﷺ did pray over him; the justification for praying over him is only that his outward appearance was the outward appearance of Islam, so Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known to him that when he knew of hypocrisy in a person, there was to be no prayer over him. ﴿وَلا تَقُمْ عَلى قَبْرِهِ﴾ (nor stand at his grave): when a dead person was buried, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to stand at his grave and supplicate for him.

zajjaj:90-90.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَجاءَ المُعَذِّرُونَ مِنَ الأعْرابِ لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ﴾ (And those with excuses among the Bedouins came, that permission might be given to them): ”اَلْمُعَذِّرُونَ“ with a doubled dhāl, and it is also read ”اَلْمُعْذِرُونَ“. Whoever reads ”اَلْمُعْذِرُونَ“, its interpretation is: those who presented an excuse (أعْذَرُوا), i.e. came with an excuse. Whoever reads ”اَلْمُعَذِّرُونَ“ with a doubled dhāl, its interpretation is ”اَلْمُعْتَذِرُونَ“ (those excusing themselves), except that the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl because of the nearness of their points of articulation. The meaning of ”اَلْمُعْتَذِرُونَ“ is: those who make excuses, whether they had an excuse or did not have one; and here it is more likely that they had an excuse. They recited:
؎إلى الحَوْلِ ثُمَّ اسْمُ السَّلامِ عَلَيْكُما ∗∗∗ ومَن يَبْكِ حَوْلًا كامِلًا فَقَدِ اعْتَذَرْ
(Until a year [has passed]; then the name of peace be upon you both — and whoever weeps a full year has [given his] excuse.)
The meaning is: he has come with an excuse. ”اَلْمُعِذِّرُونَ“, with kasra on the ʿayn, is also permissible, because the original is ”اَلْمُعْتَذِرُونَ“: the tāʾ was made quiescent and assimilated into the dhāl, and its vowel was transferred to the ʿayn, so the fatḥa became the most fitting of all; and whoever gives the ʿayn a kasra vowels it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ”اَلْمُعُذَّرُونَ“ is also permissible, by making it follow the ḍamma that precedes it. These two forms — kasra on the ʿayn and ḍamma on it — have not been read; they are only permissible in grammar, and they are two ways that make the pronunciation heavy, so reading with them is rejected. It may also be that ”اَلْمُعَذِّرُونَ“ are those who make [false] excuses (يُعَذَّرُونَ), giving the impression that they have excuses when they have no excuse.
And His saying: ﴿اسْتَأْذَنَكَ أُولُو الطَّوْلِ مِنهُمْ﴾ (the men of means among them ask your leave) [al-Tawba: 86]: it was said that ”أُولُو الطَّوْلِ“ are the people of wealth, and it was said: the people of superiority in meaning, judgment and rank. ”اَلطَّوْلُ“ is superiority in the capacity for these things.
And His saying: ﴿رَضُوا بِأنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الخَوالِفِ﴾ (They were content to be with those who stay behind) [al-Tawba: 93]: ”اَلْخَوالِفُ“ are the women; and it may also be the plural of ”خالِفَةٌ“ among men. ”اَلْخالِفُ“ is one who is not of noble stock (غَيْرُ مُنْجِبٍ). The pattern ”فَواعِلُ“ has not come for ”فاعِلٌ“ except in two words: ”فارِسٌ“ and ”فَوارِسُ“, and ”هالِكٌ“ and ”هَوالِكُ“.
[Translator's note: the source reads «يُعَذَّرُونَ» (passive form) and «أنَّ لَهم أعْذارٌ» (nominative where the accusative أعْذارًا is expected); both are translated as written.]

zajjaj:97-97.t:
And His saying: ﴿الأعْرابُ أشَدُّ كُفْرًا ونِفاقًا﴾ (The Bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy): these were Bedouins who were around Medina; their disbelief is stronger because they are harsher and coarser than the settled people, and they are also further from hearing the revelation and the warning of the Messenger.
And His saying: ﴿وَأجْدَرُ ألا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ ما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾ (and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger): ”أنْ“ is in the position of the accusative, because the bāʾ has been omitted from before ”أنْ“; the meaning is “more likely to abandon knowledge (أجْدَرُ بِتَرْكِ العِلْمِ)”. You say: “You are likely to (جَدِيرٌ أنْ) do such-and-such” and “… likely to (بِأنْ) do such-and-such,” just as you say: “You are apt to (خَلِيقٌ أنْ) do,” i.e. this act comes easily in you. When the bāʾ is omitted, it is only correct with ”أنْ“; and if you bring the bāʾ, it is correct with ”أنْ“ and with other than it. You say: ”أنْتَ جَدِيرٌ أنْ تَقُومَ“ and ”جَدِيرٌ بِالقِيامِ“; but if you said ”أنْتَ جَدِيرٌ القِيامَ“, it would be a mistake. It is only correct with ”أنْ“ because ”أنْ“ indicates the future, so it is as though it were a compensation for what was omitted.

zajjaj:98-98.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمُ الدَّوائِرَ﴾ (and he awaits for you turns of misfortune), i.e. death and being killed.

zajjaj:99-99.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُرُباتٍ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ (means of nearness with Allah): there are three forms in it: ”قُرُباتٍ“ with ḍamma on the rāʾ, ”قُرْباتٍ“ with it quiescent, and ”قُرَباتٍ“ with fatḥa on the rāʾ.
﴿وَصَلَواتِ الرَّسُولِ﴾ (and the prayers of the Messenger), and likewise ﴿وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (and pray for them) [al-Tawba: 103]: its meaning is the supplication of the Messenger. Al-Aʿshā said:
؎تَقُولُ بِنْتِي وقَدْ قَرَّبْتُ مُرْتَحِلًا ∗∗∗ يا رَبِّ جَنِّبْ أبِي الأوْصابَ والوَجَعا
(My daughter says, as I have brought near [my mount] to set out: “O Lord, keep my father away from ailments and pain.”)
؎عَلَيْكِ مِثْلُ الَّذِي صَلَّيْتِ فاغْتَمِضِي ∗∗∗ عَيْنًا فَإنَّ لِجَنْبِ الأرْضِ مُضْطَجَعا
(Upon you be the like of what you prayed for; so close your eye [in sleep], for the side of the earth is a place to lie down.)
If you wish you may say ”عَلَيْكِ مِثْلُ الَّذِي“ or ”مِثْلَ الَّذِي“. Whoever says ”عَلَيْكِ مِثْلُ الَّذِي صَلَّيْتِ“ has commanded her to supplicate, as though he said: “Supplicate the like of what you supplicated.” And whoever says ”مِثْلَ“, the meaning is: “Upon you be the like of this supplication,” i.e. “I have fixed upon you the like of this.”
[Translator's note: as printed, the source assigns the command sense (“supplicate the like…”) to the nominative ”مِثْلُ“ and the other sense to the accusative ”مِثْلَ“; the reverse would be expected, since ”عَلَيْكِ“ + accusative is the verbal-noun-of-command construction. The text is translated as written.]

zajjaj:100-100.t:
And His saying: ﴿والسّابِقُونَ الأوَّلُونَ مِنَ المُهاجِرِينَ والأنْصارِ﴾ (And the first forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers): ”والأنْصارُ“ (nominative) is also permissible. Whoever says ”والأنْصارِ“ (genitive) conjoins it to ”المُهاجِرِينَ“; the meaning is: “and the first forerunners from among the Emigrants and from among the Helpers.” Whoever says ”والأنْصارُ“ conjoins it to ”والسّابِقُونَ“, as though he said: “and the forerunners and the Helpers.”
And His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهم بِإحْسانٍ﴾ (and those who followed them in excellence), i.e. whoever follows them until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهم ورَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾ (Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him): its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is that Allah was pleased with their deeds, and that they were pleased with what Allah recompensed them with.

zajjaj:101-101.t: And His saying: ﴿وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكم مِنَ الأعْرابِ مُنافِقُونَ ومِن أهْلِ المَدِينَةِ مَرَدُوا عَلى النِّفاقِ﴾ (And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and [also] among the people of Medina; they have persisted in hypocrisy): [this involves] placing earlier and later (taqdīm and taʾkhīr): ”مَرَدُوا“ is connected with His saying ”مُنافِقُونَ“. ﴿سَنُعَذِّبُهم مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾ (We will punish them twice): i.e. We will punish them for the hypocrisy and for the deed; and it was said: with killing and with the punishment of the grave. ﴿ثُمَّ يُرَدُّونَ إلى عَذابٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ (then they will be returned to a great punishment): i.e. they will be punished in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:103-103.t: And His saying: ﴿خُذْ مِن أمْوالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهم وتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِها﴾ (Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow): it is proper for ”تُطَهِّرُهم بِها“ to be a naʿt (adjective) of ”الصَّدَقَة“, as though He said: “Take from their wealth a purifying charity.” The better view is that ”تُطَهِّرُهم“ refers to the Prophet ﷺ; the meaning is: “Take from their wealth a charity, for you purify them by it.” ”تُطَهِّرْهم“ in the jussive (jazm), as the answer to the command, is also permissible; the meaning is: “If you take from their wealth, you will purify them and cause them to grow (وتُزَكِّهِمْ).” But in the reading it is not permissible except with the yāʾ retained in ”تُزَكِّيهِمْ“, following the muṣḥaf. ﴿وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ إنَّ صَلاتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَهُمْ﴾ (and pray for them; indeed your prayer is a tranquillity for them): i.e. supplicate for them; and ”سَكَنٌ“ means: they find tranquillity through it.

zajjaj:104-104.t: And His saying: ﴿ألَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ هو يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبادِهِ ويَأْخُذُ الصَّدَقاتِ﴾ (Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities): its interpretation is “and accepts the charities.” Likewise what is related — “Charity falls into the hand of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He” — its interpretation is that Allah — exalted be His praise — accepts the charity and multiplies [the reward] for it.

zajjaj:106-106.t:
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ لأمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ (And others deferred for the command of Allah): the meaning of ”مُرْجَؤُونَ“ is “postponed.” One says ”أرْجَأْتُ الأمْرَ“ when you have postponed it. It is [also] read ﴿مُرْجَوْنَ﴾, on [the pattern of] ”أرْجَيْتُ“. ”آخَرُونَ“ is conjoined to His saying: ﴿وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكم مِنَ الأعْرابِ مُنافِقُونَ ومِن أهْلِ المَدِينَةِ﴾ (And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Medina) [al-Tawba: 101]; the meaning is: “among the people of Medina are hypocrites, and among them are others who are deferred.”
It is said that they are the three who were left behind. ﴿إمّا يُعَذِّبُهم وإمّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (either He will punish them or He will turn to them in forgiveness): ”إمّا“ is for the occurrence of one of two things. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — knows what their affair will come to, but this is for the servants: they were addressed with what they know. So the meaning is: “but their affair, in your eyes, stands thus, between fear and hope.”

zajjaj:107-107.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مَسْجِدًا ضِرارًا وكُفْرًا﴾ (And those who took a mosque for causing harm and disbelief): ”اَلَّذِينَ“ is in the position of the nominative; the meaning is: “and among them are those who took a mosque for causing harm.” ”ضِرارًا“ is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: “they took it for harm, disbelief, division and lying in wait.” When the lām was omitted, the verb reached [the noun directly] and put it in the accusative. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) construed according to the meaning, because their taking the mosque on something other than God-fearing means: “they caused harm by it, a causing of harm.” The explanation of the verse is that a group of the hypocrites of the Anṣār wanted to separate from the Prophet ﷺ those of the believers who prayed with him, so they took a mosque by which to cut off the believers and the Prophet ﷺ from the mosque of “Qubāʾ”. ﴿وَإرْصادًا لِمَن حارَبَ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾ (and as a lying-in-wait for one who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before): there was a man called Abū ʿĀmir the Monk who warred against the Prophet ﷺ and went off to Heraclius; he was one of the hypocrites. They said: “We will build this mosque and wait for Abū ʿĀmir until he comes and prays in it.” So ”اَلْإرْصادُ“ is waiting.
They took this mosque in order to cause harm and in disbelief, because obstinacy against the Prophet ﷺ is disbelief. Allah acquainted His Prophet ﷺ with their inner intention, and with the fact that they would swear falsely, so He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَلَيَحْلِفُنَّ إنْ أرَدْنا إلا الحُسْنى واللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إنَّهم لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ (And they will surely swear, “We intended nothing but good,” and Allah testifies that they are liars). They had invited the Prophet ﷺ to pray in it, so Allah — exalted be His praise — sent down: ﴿لا تَقُمْ فِيهِ أبَدًا﴾ (Do not stand in it, ever) [al-Tawba: 108]. Then Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made clear which of the two mosques was more deserving of standing in it, saying: ﴿لَمَسْجِدٌ أُسِّسَ عَلى التَّقْوى مِن أوَّلِ يَوْمٍ﴾ (A mosque founded on God-fearing from the first day) [al-Tawba: 108], by which He means the mosque of “Qubāʾ”, ﴿أحَقُّ أنْ تَقُومَ فِيهِ﴾ (is more worthy that you stand in it) [al-Tawba: 108]. ”أنْ“ is in the position of the accusative; the meaning is: “A mosque founded on God-fearing is more worthy of your standing (بِأنْ تَقُومُ) in it.” ﴿فِيهِ رِجالٌ يُحِبُّونَ أنْ يَتَطَهَّرُوا﴾ (In it are men who love to purify themselves) [al-Tawba: 108]: it is related «that the Prophet ﷺ stood at the door of the mosque and said: “Allah has praised you well concerning your purification; so with what do you purify yourselves?” They said: “We wash the trace of excrement with water.” These were a group of the Anṣār.»
[Translator's note: the source has «بِأنْ تَقُومُ» with the indicative; after «أنْ» the subjunctive «تَقُومَ» is expected. Translated as written.]

zajjaj:109-109.t:
And His saying: ﴿أفَمَن أسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ﴾ (Is then one who founded his building…): ”أفَمَن أُسِّسَ بُنْيانُهُ“ (passive) is also permissible, ”أفَمَن أساسُ بُنْيانِهِ“ is permissible, and ”أفَمَن أُسُسُ بُنْيانِهِ“ is permissible. As for ”أسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ“ and ”أُسِّسَ بُنْيانُهُ“, they are two good readings; what has been mentioned other than these two is permissible in Arabic but not permissible in reading, unless a transmission is established for it. The meaning is that one who founded his building on God-fearing is better than one who founded his building on disbelief. So He said: ﴿عَلى شَفا جُرُفٍ هارٍ﴾ (on the edge of a crumbling bank). ”شَفا الشَّيْءِ“ is its brink and its edge. ”اَلشَّفا“ is maqṣūr (ending in short alif), written with alif, and its dual is ”شَفَوَيْنِ“. The meaning of ”هارٍ“ is ”هائِرٍ“ (crumbling); this is of the metathesized (maqlūb) [forms], as they said of ”لاثَ الشَّيْءُ“, when it goes around, that it is ”لاثٍ“, the original being ”لائِثٌ“; and as they said ”شاكِ السِّلاحِ“ and ”شائِكُ“. The poet said:
؎فَتَعَرَّفُونِي إنَّنِي أنا ذاكُمُ ∗∗∗ شاكٍ سِلاحِي في الحَوادِثِ مُعْلِمُ
(So recognize me: I am that one of yours, my weapons bristling, marked out [for valour] in the events.)
And as al-ʿAjjāj said:
؎لاثٍ بِهِ الأشاءُ والعُبْرِيُّ
(Around it wind the young palms and the riverside lote-trees.)
”اَلْأشاءُ“ is palm trees, and ”اَلْعُبْرِيُّ“ is the lote-tree that is on the banks of rivers; the meaning of ”لاثٍ بِهِ“ is “surrounding it.” ﴿فانْهارَ بِهِ في نارِ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ (so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell): this is a parable; the meaning is that the building of this mosque, which was built for harm and disbelief, is like a building on the bank of Hell which tumbles down with its people into it.

zajjaj:110-110.t: And His saying: ﴿لا يَزالُ بُنْيانُهُمُ الَّذِي بَنَوْا رِيبَةً في قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ (Their building which they built will not cease to be a [cause of] doubt in their hearts): some said: “will not cease to be disbelief,” and some said: “will not cease to be doubt.” ”اَلرِّيبَةُ“ is from ”اَلرَّيْبُ“, and ”اَلرَّيْبُ“ is doubt. So Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that as for their building, they will not cease to be in doubt about it. It is possible that Allah — exalted be His praise — made their punishment that He bound error upon them because they embarked on this grave matter. ﴿إلا أنْ تَقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ (unless their hearts are cut to pieces): ”إلّا أنْ يَقْطَعَ قُلُوبَهم“ is also permissible; its meaning is “unless they die.” Some said: unless they repent with a repentance by which their hearts are cut to pieces with remorse and grief over their negligence.

zajjaj:111-111.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرى مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ أنْفُسَهم وأمْوالَهم بِأنَّ لَهُمُ الجَنَّةَ﴾ (Allah has purchased from the believers their selves and their wealth [in exchange] for that theirs is Paradise): it is related that He traded with them and made the price high for them. This is like what He said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلالَةَ بِالهُدى فَما رَبِحَتْ تِجارَتُهُمْ﴾ (Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance, so their trade has not profited) [al-Baqara: 16]. ﴿يُقاتِلُونَ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَيَقْتُلُونَ ويُقْتَلُونَ وعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا﴾ (They fight in the way of Allah, and they kill and are killed — a promise binding upon Him in truth): [وعْدًا is accusative] according to the meaning, because the meaning of His saying ﴿بِأنَّ لَهُمُ الجَنَّةَ﴾ is: He promised them Paradise, a promise binding on Him in truth. If it were outside the Qur'an, the nominative would be permissible, in the sense of “that is a promise binding on Him, true.”
And His saying: ﴿فِي التَّوْراةِ والإنْجِيلِ والقُرْآنِ﴾ (in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an) indicates that the people of every religious community were commanded to fight, and were promised Paradise for it.

zajjaj:112-112.t:
And His saying: ﴿التّائِبُونَ العابِدُونَ﴾ (Those who repent, those who worship): its nominative case may properly be on several grounds. One of them is praise (madḥ), as though He said: “these are those who repent” or “they are those who repent.” It may also be by way of badal (substitute); the meaning is “those who repent fight” — and this is the view of the philologists. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: What I hold — and Allah knows best — is that His saying ﴿التّائِبُونَ العابِدُونَ﴾ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is implied; the meaning is: “Those who repent, those who worship … — to the end of the verse — theirs is Paradise too,” i.e. [this includes] one who did not fight, not out of obstinacy nor intending to abandon fighting, because some Muslims suffice on behalf of others in fighting; so whoever has this description, his is Paradise too. ”اَلتّائِبُونَ“ are those who repented from disbelief; ”اَلْعابِدُونَ“ are those who worshipped Allah alone; ”اَلرّاكِعُونَ السّاجِدُونَ“ (those who bow, those who prostrate) are those who performed what Allah made obligatory on them in bowing and prostration; ﴿الآمِرُونَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾ (those who enjoin what is right): those who enjoin faith in Allah; ﴿والنّاهُونَ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ﴾ (and those who forbid what is wrong): [who forbid] disbelief in Allah. It may also be: “those who enjoin all that is right and forbid all that is wrong.” ﴿والحافِظُونَ لِحُدُودِ اللَّهِ﴾ (and those who keep the limits of Allah): those who carry out what Allah has commanded.
And His saying: ﴿السّائِحُونَ﴾ (those who travel/fast): according to the statement of the philologists and the exegetes alike, [it means] those who fast. The view of al-Ḥasan is that they are those who fast the obligatory [fast]; and it has been said that they are those who fast continually. Al-Ḥasan's statement on this is clearer. Likewise ”اَلرّاكِعُونَ السّاجِدُونَ“, according to al-Ḥasan, are those who perform what has been made obligatory on them in their bowing and prostration.

zajjaj:113-113.t:
And His saying: ﴿ما كانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ ولَوْ كانُوا أُولِي قُرْبى﴾ (It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they are relatives): it is related «that the Prophet ﷺ offered Islam to his uncle Abū Ṭālib at the time of his death, and mentioned to him the obligation of [Abū Ṭālib's] right over him, but Abū Ṭālib refused. So the Prophet ﷺ said: “I will surely ask forgiveness for you until I am forbidden from that.”» It is related that he asked forgiveness for his mother, and it is related that he asked forgiveness for his father; and that the believers mentioned the good qualities of their fathers in the Jāhiliyya and asked to seek forgiveness for their fathers because of the good qualities they had. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that this is not permissible, and said: ﴿ما كانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ ولَوْ كانُوا أُولِي قُرْبى﴾.
And His saying: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهم أنَّهم أصْحابُ الجَحِيمِ﴾ (after it has become clear to them that they are the companions of Hellfire), i.e. after it has become clear to them that they died as disbelievers.

zajjaj:114-114.t:
Then He — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known how Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father was, saying: ﴿وَما كانَ اسْتِغْفارُ إبْراهِيمَ لأبِيهِ إلا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وعَدَها إيّاهُ﴾ (And Abraham's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him). It is related that he had promised him to seek forgiveness for him during the days of his life; and it is related that Abraham's father had promised Abraham that he would accept Islam if he sought forgiveness for him. When it became clear to him that he persisted in disbelief, he disowned him. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿قَدْ كانَتْ لَكم أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ في إبْراهِيمَ والَّذِينَ مَعَهُ﴾ (There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him) [al-Mumtaḥana: 4], up to His saying: ﴿إلا قَوْلَ إبْراهِيمَ لأبِيهِ لأسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ﴾ (except the saying of Abraham to his father, “I will surely ask forgiveness for you”) [al-Mumtaḥana: 4], i.e. [do not] take Abraham as an example in this saying.
And His saying: ﴿إنَّ إبْراهِيمَ لأوّاهٌ حَلِيمٌ﴾ (Indeed Abraham was awwāh and forbearing): it is related «that ʿUmar asked the Prophet ﷺ about al-awwāh, and he said: “Al-awwāh is the one who supplicates much (الدَّعّاءُ).”» ”اَلْأوّاهُ“ in most of the transmission is the one who supplicates much. It is related that al-awwāh is the one with understanding [of religion] (al-faqīh); it is related that al-awwāh is the believer, in the language of Abyssinia; and it is related that al-awwāh is the merciful, the gentle. Abū ʿUbayda said: ”اَلْأوّاهُ“ is one who sighs (المُتَأوِّهُ) out of compassion and out of fear, who humbles himself in supplication with certainty — he means that his humble supplication is with certainty of being answered, and with adherence to obedience. Abū ʿUbayda's statement has gathered most of what has been related concerning al-awwāh. Abū ʿUbayda recited:
؎إذا ما قُمْتُ أرْحَلُها بِلَيْلٍ ∗∗∗ تَأوَّهُ آهَةَ الرَّجُلِ الحَزِينِ
(Whenever I rise to saddle her by night, she sighs the sigh of a grieving man.)
[Translator's note: «أيْ: تَأسَّوْا بِإبْراهِيمَ في هَذا القَوْلِ» literally reads “i.e. take Abraham as an example in this saying”; since the verse excepts this saying from the example, the sense is that this saying is not to be imitated. The word “[do not]” has been supplied.]

zajjaj:115-115.t: And His saying: ﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْمًا بَعْدَ إذْ هَداهم حَتّى يُبَيِّنَ لَهم ما يَتَّقُونَ﴾ (And Allah would not lead a people astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should guard against): it is related that when the prohibition of wine was revealed and the ḥadd punishments were instituted, the Muslims said concerning those who had died before that and had not reached the prohibition: “Ask about their state.” So Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that He does not take them to account for what was prohibited [later] of what had not been prohibited to them. It may also be [the meaning]: “When Allah grants success in guidance, there is no leading astray after it,” because whomever Allah guides, there is none to lead him astray.

zajjaj:117-117.t: And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ تابَ اللَّهُ عَلى النَّبِيِّ والمُهاجِرِينَ والأنْصارِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ في ساعَةِ العُسْرَةِ﴾ (Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship): its meaning is: at the time of hardship, because ”السّاعَةُ“ applies to any period of time. At that time there was intense heat, and the people were in severe straits: a camel was shared among a group who took turns riding it, and such was their hardship and poverty that sometimes two would divide a date between them, and sometimes a group would suck on a date so as to drink water after it, and sometimes they slaughtered camels and drank from the water of their stomachs because of the heat. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that He had turned to them in forgiveness after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated, i.e. after they had almost turned back from their campaign because of the hardship — not that [the heart] would deviate from faith; it is only that they almost returned. So Allah turned to them by bringing them back from their campaign.

zajjaj:118-118.t: And His saying: ﴿وَعَلى الثَّلاثَةِ الَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا﴾ (and to the three who were left behind): the meaning is: “and He turned in forgiveness to the three who were left behind.” It is said that they are the ones deferred for the command of Allah.

zajjaj:119-119.t: And His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وكُونُوا مَعَ الصّادِقِينَ﴾ (O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful): following the sequence of the discourse, it indicates that they were commanded to be with the Prophet ﷺ in hardship and ease. And His saying — and Allah knows best — may be [understood] on this [basis]: ﴿مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ رِجالٌ صَدَقُوا ما عاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ (Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah) [al-Aḥzāb: 23]. It has been transmitted from some of them [as] ”مِنَ الصّادِقِينَ“ (of the truthful), and the meaning is the same. It may also be: “among those who are truthful and do not lie, in word or in deed.”

zajjaj:120-120.t: And His saying: ﴿لا يُصِيبُهم ظَمَأٌ ولا نَصَبٌ﴾ (no thirst or fatigue afflicts them): ”اَلظَّمَأُ“ is thirst and ”اَلنَّصَبُ“ is fatigue. ﴿وَلا مَخْمَصَةٌ﴾ (nor hunger): ”اَلْمَخْمَصَةُ“ is famine. So Allah made known that He will recompense them for all of that, and that He records for them a righteous deed.

zajjaj:122-122.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَما كانَ المُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كافَّةً﴾ (And it is not for the believers to go forth all together): this is the wording of a statement containing the meaning of a command, as was ﴿ما كانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ (It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists) [al-Tawba: 113]. The meaning is that whenever there was a raiding party (sariyya), they would go forth in it all of them together; so Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that some of them ought to go forth and some remain with the Prophet ﷺ, so that he would not remain alone, and so that those of them who went out would not be left without benefit from him. So He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿فَلَوْلا نَفَرَ مِن كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ مِنهم طائِفَةٌ لِيَتَفَقَّهُوا في الدِّينِ﴾ (Why then does not a party from every group of them go forth, so that they may gain understanding in the religion?). The meaning is that if some of them remained in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ and heard revelation from him, they would teach those who had gone forth what they had learned, so they would be equal in knowledge and not be without it. It is possible — and Allah knows best — that this is evidence that jihad is an obligation in which one group suffices on behalf of another group.
﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ يَلُونَكم مِنَ الكُفّارِ ولْيَجِدُوا فِيكم غِلْظَةً﴾ (O you who believe, fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you, and let them find harshness in you) [al-Tawba: 123]: ”غِلْظَةً“ has three dialectal forms: ”غِلْظَةً“, ”غُلْظَةً“ and ”غَلْظَةً“. This is evidence that the people of every frontier ought to fight those adjacent to them. It was said that the Arabs are meant by this. And it was said that the Prophet ﷺ would sometimes, in his warfare, pass over the enemies adjacent to him, so that this would make him more awe-inspiring; so he was commanded to fight those adjacent to him, so that this would be followed as a practice (sunna).
And His saying: ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ المُتَّقِينَ﴾ (And know that Allah is with the God-fearing) [al-Tawba: 123], i.e. Allah commands (آمِرٌ) whoever helped Him in warfare.
[Translator's note: «اَللَّهُ آمِرٌ مَن نَصَرَهُ بِالحَرْبِ» is translated as it stands; the context suggests «ناصِرٌ» (helps) may have been intended, i.e. “Allah helps whoever …”.]

zajjaj:124-124.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإذا ما أُنْـزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ فَمِنهم مَن يَقُولُ أيُّكم زادَتْهُ هَذِهِ إيمانًا﴾ (And whenever a sura is sent down, among them is one who says, “Which of you has this increased in faith?”): He attributed the faith to the sura because it increases on account of it.

zajjaj:125-125.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأمّا الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ (But as for those in whose hearts is a disease), i.e. doubt and hypocrisy, it increased them in filth added to their filth, i.e. it increased them in disbelief added to their disbelief, because whenever they disbelieved in a sura, their disbelief increased.

zajjaj:126-126.t: And His saying: ﴿أوَلا يَرَوْنَ أنَّهم يُفْتَنُونَ في كُلِّ عامٍ مَرَّةً أوْ مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾ (Do they not see that they are tried every year once or twice?): its meaning is: they are tested every year. It was said: they are tested by the call to jihad; and it was said: they are tested in that punishment and hardship descend upon them.

zajjaj:127-127.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإذا ما أُنْـزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ نَظَرَ بَعْضُهم إلى بَعْضٍ﴾ (And whenever a sura is sent down, they look at one another): they say that by gesture, because they are hypocrites and do not show it openly. ﴿هَلْ يَراكم مِن أحَدٍ﴾ (“Does anyone see you?”): they say that secretly, guarding against Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — making them known, and He knows best. ﴿ثُمَّ انْصَرَفُوا﴾ (then they turn away), i.e. they do that and turn away. It may be that they turn away from the place in which they hid, and it may be that they turn away from acting upon anything of what they hear. ﴿صَرَفَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ (Allah has turned their hearts away), i.e. Allah led them astray, as a requital for their deed.

zajjaj:128-128.t: And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ جاءَكم رَسُولٌ مِن أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ (There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves), i.e. he is a human being like you; i.e. this is more binding as an argument against you, because you understand from one who is like you. It may be that He meant by it that he is an Arab, just as you are Arabs, so you know him by experience and are acquainted with his way. ﴿عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ ما عَنِتُّمْ﴾ (grievous to him is what you suffer), i.e. your suffering is grievous to him; ”اَلْعَنَتُ“ is meeting with hardship. ﴿حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ (concerned over you), i.e. eager for your faith.

zajjaj:129-129.t:
﴿فَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقُلْ حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ﴾ (But if they turn away, say: “Allah is sufficient for me”), i.e. the One who suffices me is Allah. ﴿عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وهو رَبُّ العَرْشِ العَظِيمِ﴾ (upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne): and ”اَلْعَظِيمُ“ — both [cases] are permissible here.
[Translator's note: the source says only «و”اَلْعَظِيمُ“، هَهُنا جائِزانِ»; the two permissible forms are presumably the genitive «العَظِيمِ» (describing the Throne) and the nominative «العَظِيمُ» (describing the Lord).]
And His saying: ﴿مِن أوَّلِ يَوْمٍ﴾ (from the first day) [al-Tawba: 108]: ”مِن“ has entered upon time, whereas the basic [particles for this] are ”مُنْذُ“ and ”مُذْ“; this is the more frequent usage for time. ”مِن“ may enter [upon time] because it is the basic particle for the starting point of an extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya) and for partition (tabʿīḍ). Like this is the saying of Zuhayr:
؎لِمَنِ الدِّيارُ بِقُنَّةِ الحِجْرِ ∗∗∗ أقْوَيْنَ مِن حِجَجٍ ومِن شَهْرِ
(Whose are the dwellings on the summit of al-Ḥijr, deserted for years and for a month?)
And it was said that the meaning of this is: “since years and since
[Translator's note: the source text breaks off here, mid-sentence.]

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Barāʾa
His words — Majestic and Mighty —: ﴿بَراءَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ﴾. «Ubayy ibn Kaʿb was asked: Why was "Barāʾa" not opened with "بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ"? He said: "Because it was revealed among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give orders at the beginning of every sūra for "بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ", but he did not order that for Sūrat Barāʾa, so it was joined to Sūrat al-Anfāl because of its resemblance to it."» He means that the matter of covenants is mentioned in Sūrat al-Anfāl, and this one was revealed concerning the breaking of covenants, so it was bound up with al-Anfāl in resemblance.
Abū Isḥāq said: One of our companions informed us from our colleague Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Mubarrad that he said: It was not opened with "بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ" because "بِسْمِ اللَّهِ" is an opening for good, while the beginning of Barāʾa is a threat and the breaking of covenants; that is why it was not opened with "بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ".
Barāʾa was revealed in the year nine of the Hijra. Mecca was conquered in the year eight, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed ʿAttāb ibn Usayd to lead the people at the standing during the pilgrimage season; in that year Muslims and idolaters came together at the place of standing and at the sites and rites of the Ḥajj. When it was the year nine, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq to lead the people at the standing, ordered that Barāʾa be recited, and assigned its recitation to ʿAlī, saying about that: «None shall convey on my behalf except a man from me.» That is because the custom of the Arabs in concluding their pacts and breaking them was that a man from the tribe should undertake that on the tribe's behalf; so it would have been possible for the Arabs, when the breaking of the covenant on the Messenger's behalf was recited to them, to say: "This is contrary to what we know among ourselves regarding the breaking of covenants." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ removed this pretext, and Barāʾa was recited at the place of standing: ﴿بَراءَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ إلى الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ﴾, that is: He has become free of granting them covenants and of keeping faith with them, that being because they broke faith.
"بَراءَةٌ" is nominative in two ways. One of them is as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), with the meaning: "These verses are an immunity from Allah and His Messenger." The other is as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being "إلى الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ", because "بَراءَةٌ" is connected with "مِن", and it becomes like your saying "اَلْقَصْدُ إلى زَيْدٍ" (the aim is towards Zayd) and "اَلتَّبَرُّؤُ إلَيْكَ" (the disavowal is to you). Both are permissible and good. One says: "بَرِئْتُ مِنَ الرَّجُلِ، والدِّينِ، بَراءَةً" (I became free of the man and of the religion), and "بَرِئْتُ مِنَ المَرَضِ" (I recovered from the illness), and also "بَرَأْتُ بُرْءًا"; they have also transmitted "بَرَأْتُ، أبْرُؤُ، بُرُوءًا". We have not found, among verbs whose final radical is hamza, "فَعَلْتُ، أفْعُلُ", like "قَرَأْتُ، أقْرُؤُ" and "هَنَأْتُ البَعِيرَ، أهْنُؤُهُ". «[Translator's note: the sentence is translated as transmitted; the examples cited seem to illustrate the pattern rather than exclude it, and the sense intended is presumably that this pattern is not attested for such verbs apart from بَرَأْتُ أبْرُؤُ.]»
Scholars of the language investigated this thoroughly and found it only in this word. One says "بَرَيْتُ القَلَمَ" (I sharpened the pen), and for everything you whittle "أبْرِيهِ بَرْيًا", without hamza; likewise "بَراةُ السَّيْرِ" (the shavings of the leather strap), without hamza. "اَلْبُرَةُ" is a ring of iron in the she-camel's nose; if it is of hair it is a "خِزامَةٌ", and that which is in the camel's nose of wood is called "اَلْخِشاشُ". One says "أبْرَيْتُ النّاقَةَ، أبْرِيها، بِراءً" when I put a بُرَة on her, and it is said only with the alif: "أبْرَيْتُ"; whereas from "اَلْخِزامَةُ" one says "خَزَمْتُ" without the alif, and likewise from "اَلْخِشاشُ" "خَشَشْتُ". "اَلْبُرَةُ" is also the anklet, from this. "اَلْبَرَةُ" is pluralised as "بُرِينُ" and "اَلْبُرى".

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His words — Majestic and Mighty —: ﴿وَإنْ نَكَثُوا أيْمانَهم مِن بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ وطَعَنُوا في دِينِكم فَقاتِلُوا أئِمَّةَ الكُفْرِ﴾, that is: the chiefs of the disbelievers and their leaders, because the imām is the one who is followed. This verse requires the killing of the dhimmī (protected non-Muslim) if he openly attacks Islam, because the covenant is concluded with him on condition that he does not attack it; if he attacks it, he has broken it.
His words: ﴿أئِمَّةَ الكُفْرِ﴾ — according to the grammarians there is a single form in it: "أيِمَّةَ", with a hamza and a yāʾ. The readers read "أئِمَّةَ" with two hamzas, and "أيِمَّةَ" with a hamza and a yāʾ. As for the grammarians, they do not permit the combination of the two hamzas here, because they do not come together in one word; whoever reads "أئِمَّةَ" with two hamzas ought to read "يا بَنِي أأْدَمَ", whereas the consensus is that "آدَمَ" has a single hamza. So the disagreement returns to the consensus. However, the grammarians find this question difficult and hold more than one view on it. When we prefer one man over another in leadership (imāma), they say: "هَذا أوَمُّ مِن هَذا", and some of them say: "أيَمُّ مِن هَذا". The original form in the language is "أأْمِمَةٌ", because it is the plural of "إمامٌ", like "مِثالٌ" and "أمْثِلَةٌ"; but when the two mīms came together, the first was assimilated into the second and its vowel was thrown onto the hamza, so it became "أئِمَّةَ". The grammarians then replaced the hamza with yāʾ. Whoever says "هَذا أيَمُّ مِن هَذا" replaces this hamza with a yāʾ whenever it takes a vowel. Abū Isḥāq said: For the one who said "هَذا أوَمُّ مِن هَذا", its original form was "أأمُّ"; he could not replace it with an alif because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, so he made it a wāw with fatḥa, because he said: when you pluralise "آدَمُ" you say "أوادِمُ". And this is the analogy of the one who made it yāʾ; he said: the yāʾ in "أئِمَّةٌ" has become a fixed substitute. This is the school of al-Akhfash, and the first is the school of al-Māzinī. Abū Isḥāq said: I think it is the more analogical of the two ways — I mean "هَذا أوَمُّ مِن هَذا". As for "أئِمَّةٌ" with two hamzas combined, it is not among the schools of our colleagues, except for what is reported from Ibn Isḥāq «[Translator's note: so in the text; probably Ibn Abī Isḥāq is meant.]», who liked combining them. But that is not permissible in my view, because in this word "أئِمَّةٌ" doubling and assimilation have occurred; when it was assimilated, a change affected the letter and its vowel was thrown onto the hamza, so leaving it is evidence that it is a hamza that has received the vowel of what follows it. On this analogy, "هَذا أأمُّ مِن هَذا" is permissible. What we began with is the preferred choice: that two hamzas should not be combined.
His words: ﴿إنَّهم لا أيْمانَ لَهُمْ﴾ — it is also read "لا إيمانَ لَهم". Whoever reads "لا أيْمانَ لَهم" with fatḥa has described them as breaking the covenant, and this is the better of the two readings. Whoever reads "لا إيمانَ لَهم" has described them as apostates, that is: "they have no Islam." It is also possible that He negated faith of them because they did not believe, as you say: "لا عِلْمَ لِفُلانٍ" (so-and-so has no knowledge).
It is also possible that "لا أيْمانَ لَهم" means: if you have granted them safety and they then break their covenant with you, the safety you gave them is void; that is, "لا إيمانَ لَهم" in the sense of "آمَنتُ إيمانًا" (I granted safety), as a maṣdar (verbal noun). ﴿لَعَلَّهم يَنْتَهُونَ﴾, that is: so that their desisting may be hoped for. النَّكْثُ is breaking, in everything.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His words — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿ألا تُقاتِلُونَ قَوْمًا﴾ — this is by way of rebuke, and its meaning is urging them to fight them. About His words ﴿وَهم بَدَءُوكم أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ it was said that they had fought the allies of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
His words: ﴿أتَخْشَوْنَهُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: "Do you fear that some harm will befall you from fighting them?" ﴿فاللَّهُ أحَقُّ أنْ تَخْشَوْهُ﴾, that is: the harm of Allah's punishment is more deserving to be feared. ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is: believing in Allah's punishment and reward.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His words: ﴿وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — in it is an indication that their anger for the sake of Allah — Mighty and Majestic — had become intense, so in this verse Allah promised victory. In it is also a proof establishing prophethood, because He — Mighty and Majestic — said: ﴿قاتِلُوهم يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ بِأيْدِيكم ويُخْزِهِمْ ويَنْصُرْكم عَلَيْهِمْ ويَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾; so Allah promised them victory and fulfilled it, and this pointed to the truth of what the Prophet ﷺ brought. His words — Exalted is He —: ﴿وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلى مَن يَشاءُ﴾ [al-Tawba: 15] are not an apodosis to His words ﴿قاتِلُوهُمْ﴾; rather it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), because "يَتُوبُ" is not of the kind of thing with which "قاتِلُوهم" can be answered.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His words: ﴿فَسِيحُوا في الأرْضِ أرْبَعَةَ أشْهُرٍ﴾, that is: go about, come and go, for four months. ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّكم غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي اللَّهِ﴾, that is: even if you are given a respite of these four months, you will not escape Allah. ﴿وَأنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْزِي الكافِرِينَ﴾ — the better is fatḥa on "أنَّ", with the meaning: "Know that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers." Kasra on it is also possible, in the sense of a resumption (istiʾnāf). This is a guarantee from Allah — Mighty and Majestic — of His giving the believers victory over the disbelievers.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
﴿وَأذانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ﴾ is conjoined to "بَراءَةٌ", and its meaning is: "and a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger." One says "آذَنْتُهُ بِالشَّيْءِ" when I have informed him of it. ﴿إلى النّاسِ يَوْمَ الحَجِّ الأكْبَرِ أنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ﴾ — it was said that "the day of the greater pilgrimage" is the day of ʿArafa, and that "the greater pilgrimage" is the standing at ʿArafa; and it was said that "the lesser pilgrimage" is the ʿumra.
There is consensus that whoever misses the standing at ʿArafa has missed the Ḥajj. Some said: it was only called "the day of the greater pilgrimage" because the festivals of the people of the religions coincided on it — the festival of the Christians, the Jews and the Magians happened to coincide on that day. But it would not be called "the day of the greater pilgrimage" for this reason, since these are festivals of non-Muslims, in which there is only the glorification of disbelief in Allah, so they have nothing at all to do with the greater pilgrimage; the Muslims are agreed that the standing at ʿArafa is the greatest part of the Ḥajj.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His words: ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ﴾ — "اَلَّذِينَ" is in the position of the accusative; that is: the disavowal falls upon the covenant-holders who broke the covenants, except those of the idolaters with whom you made a covenant, ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنْقُصُوكم شَيْئًا ولَمْ يُظاهِرُوا عَلَيْكم أحَدًا فَأتِمُّوا إلَيْهِمْ عَهْدَهم إلى مُدَّتِهِمْ﴾, that is: they are not included in the disavowal so long as they do not break the covenants.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His words: ﴿فَإذا انْسَلَخَ الأشْهُرُ الحُرُمُ فاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾, that is: kill those who broke the covenant, whose covenant has been cancelled, and who have been permitted this period. It is said that the four months were: twenty of Dhū al-Ḥijja, al-Muḥarram, Ṣafar, Rabīʿ al-Awwal and ten of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir, because the disavowal took place on the day of ʿArafa, so that time was the beginning of the term. ﴿واقْعُدُوا لَهم كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ﴾ — Abū ʿUbayda said: the meaning is "every road". Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash said: "عَلى" is omitted; the meaning is: "lie in wait for them at every place of ambush," and he recited:
نُغالِي اللَّحْمَ لِلْأضْيافِ نَيْئًا ∗∗∗ ونُرْخِصُهُ إذا نَضِجَ القُدُورُ
(We pay dearly for meat for the guests while it is raw, and make it cheap when the pots have cooked.)
The meaning is "نُغالِي بِاللَّحْمِ"; the bāʾ was omitted here, and likewise "عَلى" was omitted. Abū Isḥāq said: "كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ" is an adverb (ẓarf), as in your saying "ذَهَبْتُ مَذْهَبًا", "ذَهَبْتُ طَرِيقًا" and "ذَهَبْتُ كُلَّ طَرِيقٍ"; you need not say anything about this other than what you say about adverbs such as "خَلْفَ", "أمامَ" and "قُدّامَ".
His words: ﴿فَإخْوانُكم في الدِّينِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 11], that is: if they repent and believe, they are like you; their faith and repentance have warded off from them the sin of their disbelief and of their breaking the covenants.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His words: ﴿وَإنْ أحَدٌ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ اسْتَجارَكَ فَأجِرْهُ حَتّى يَسْمَعَ كَلامَ اللَّهِ﴾ — the meaning is: if one of them asks you to grant him protection from being killed until he hears the word of Allah, then grant him protection until he hears the word of Allah, then convey him to his place of safety. ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم قَوْمٌ لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, that is: "the matter is that," that is: "it is necessary that they be made to know, and that they be dealt with according to their ignorance and according to what makes Islam clear to them." «[Translator's note: the last phrase, وبِما يَتَبَيَّنُونَ الإسْلامَ, is translated as transmitted; its wording is somewhat unclear.]»
As for the i'rab of "أحَدٌ" with "إنْ": it is nominative by an implied (muḍmar) verb, which the overt one explains; the meaning is: "وإنِ اسْتَجارَكَ أحَدٌ" (if anyone seeks your protection). Whoever claims that "أحَدٌ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) is mistaken, because the condition (jazāʾ) does not pass over what is made nominative as a mubtadaʾ and govern what comes after it.
If you made the imperfect verb overt, you would say: "إنْ أحَدٌ يَقُمْ أُكْرِمْهُ" (if anyone stands, I will honour him). But "إنْ يَقُمْ أحَدٌ زَيْدٌ يَقُمْ" is not permissible: it is not permissible to make زَيْد nominative by an implied verb explained by the overt one and put the verb in the jussive. This was permitted with "إنْ" only because "إنْ" necessarily requires a verb, while the apodosis of the condition may be a verb or something else; and it is not permissible to imply and make the jussive after the mubtadaʾ, because you say here: "إنْ تَأْتِنِي فَزَيْدٌ يَقُومُ" (if you come to me, then Zayd will stand), so the position is the position of a mubtadaʾ. The separation is permitted only in the case of "إنْ" because "إنْ" is the mother of the conditional particles and does not depart from it to something else. As for its sisters, that is not permissible with them except in poetry. ʿAdī ibn Zayd said:
فَمَتى واغِلٌ يَزُرْهم يَحْبُو ∗∗∗ هُ وتُعْطَفْ عَلَيْهِ كَأْسُ السّاقِي
(Whenever an uninvited guest visits them, they present him with gifts, and the cup-bearer's cup is turned towards him.)

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His words: ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ عِنْدَ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ﴾, that is: the covenant is only for those who have not broken faith. ﴿فَما اسْتَقامُوا لَكم فاسْتَقِيمُوا لَهُمْ﴾, that is: as long as they persist in keeping their covenant. The position of "اَلَّذِينَ" is accusative by exception.
His words: ﴿كَيْفَ وإنْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكم لا يَرْقُبُوا فِيكم إلا ولا ذِمَّةً﴾ [al-Tawba: 8] — with "كَيْفَ" the clause "يَكُونُ لَهم عَهْدٌ" (they have a covenant) is omitted, because it has been mentioned before that. The poet said, lamenting a brother of his who had died:
وَخَبَّرْتُمانِي أنَّما المَوْتُ بِالقُرى ∗∗∗ فَكَيْفَ وهاتا هَضْبَةٌ وقَلِيبُ
(You two told me that death is only in the towns — so how, when here are but a hill and a well?)
that is: so how did he die, when he was not in a town? Similar to it is the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
وَكَيْفَ ولَمْ أعْلَمْهُمُ خَذَلُوكُمُ ∗∗∗ عَلى مُعْظَمٍ ولا أدِيمَكُمُ قَدُّوا
(And how, when I have not known them to forsake you in any grave matter, nor to have cut your hide?)
that is: so how can you blame me for praising a people while you disparage them? He dispensed with mentioning "that" along with "كَيْفَ", because something had occurred earlier in the ode that indicates what is implied.
Abū ʿUbayda said: "اَلْإلُّ" is the covenant, and "اَلذِّمَّةُ" is that which one would be blamed for neglecting. Someone else said: "اَلذِّمَّةُ" is the covenant. More than one view has been stated about "اَلْإلُّ": it was said that "اَلْإلُّ" is kinship; it was said that it is alliance; it was said that it is the covenant; and it was said that "اَلْإلُّ" is one of the names of Allah. In our view this last is not the right way, because the names of Allah — Majestic and Mighty — are known and established, as they have been heard in the Qur'an and recited in the reports. Allah — Majestic and Mighty — said: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ الأسْماءُ الحُسْنى فادْعُوهُ بِها﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 180]; so the one who supplicates says: "يا اَللَّهُ، يا رَحْمَنُ، يا رَبُّ، يا مُؤْمِنُ، يا مُهَيْمِنُ", but "يا إلُّ" has not been heard in supplication. The true sense of "اَلْإلُّ" in my view, according to what the language suggests, is the sharpening (taḥdīd) of a thing. From that is "اَلْإلَّةُ", the spear-blade, because it is sharpened; and from that is "أُذُنٌ مُؤَلَّلَةٌ" (a pointed ear), when it is sharp. "اَلْألُّ" is derived on this basis in all that has been explained of covenant and protection, and likewise kinship. When you say of a covenant "بَيْنَهُما إلٌّ", its meaning is a protection that borders closely on a person; and when you say it of kinship, its interpretation is the near kinship that borders closely on a person.

zajjaj:16-16.t: His words: ﴿أمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أنْ تُتْرَكُوا ولَمّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا مِنكُمْ﴾ — Allah — Majestic and Mighty — knew, before commanding them to fight, who would fight and who would not; but He knew that as something unseen, and here He meant the knowledge on the basis of which requital is made, because He — Majestic and Mighty — requites only according to what they have done. Sūrat Barāʾa used to be called "al-Ḥāfira" (the one that digs), because it dug into the hearts of the hypocrites. That is because when fighting was made obligatory, the hypocrite became distinct from others, and the one who allies himself with the believers from the one who allies himself with their enemies. So He — Majestic and Mighty — said: ﴿أمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أنْ تُتْرَكُوا ولَمّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا مِنكم ولَمْ يَتَّخِذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ولا رَسُولِهِ ولا المُؤْمِنِينَ ولِيجَةً﴾. "اَلْوَلِيجَةُ" is the intimate confidant (biṭāna); it is taken from "وَلَجَ الشَّيْءُ، يَلِجُ" when a thing enters; that is: they did not take between themselves and the disbelievers any inward bond of affection.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His words: ﴿ما كانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ أنْ يَعْمُرُوا مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ شاهِدِينَ عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ بِالكُفْرِ﴾ — "شاهِدِينَ" is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: it was not for them to maintain the Sacred Mosque while they were acknowledging disbelief. ﴿أُولَئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أعْمالُهُمْ﴾, that is: their disbelief has done away with the reward of their deeds.

zajjaj:18-18.t: His words: ﴿إنَّما يَعْمُرُ مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ مَن آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ وأقامَ الصَّلاةَ وآتى الزَّكاةَ ولَمْ يَخْشَ إلا اللَّهَ﴾ — the Messenger is not mentioned in this, because there is an indication of it in His words "وَأقامَ الصَّلاةَ", the prayer whose precise form the Messenger brought. "وَلَمْ يَخْشَ إلّا اللَّهَ" — its interpretation is: he feared none but Allah in the matter of religion. ﴿فَعَسى أُولَئِكَ أنْ يَكُونُوا مِنَ المُهْتَدِينَ﴾ — "عَسى" (perhaps), from Allah, is binding.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His words: ﴿أجَعَلْتُمْ سِقايَةَ الحاجِّ وعِمارَةَ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ كَمَن آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ وجاهَدَ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لا يَسْتَوُونَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ — the meaning is: "Have you made those who provide water for the pilgrims and those who maintain the Sacred Mosque like one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives?" People have disagreed about the explanation of this verse. It was said that the idolaters asked the Jews, saying: "We are the providers of water for the pilgrims and the maintainers of the Sacred Mosque; are we better, or Muḥammad and his Companions?" The Jews said to them — out of obstinacy towards the Prophet ﷺ —: "You are better." And it was said that the Muslims who strove in jihād vied in boasting … «[Translator's note: the sentence continues in the following entry (9:20).]»

zajjaj:20-20.t: … with those who had not emigrated and had not striven; so Allah — Majestic and Mighty — made known that those who strive and those who emigrate are greater in rank with Allah, and said: ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وهاجَرُوا وجاهَدُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأمْوالِهِمْ وأنْفُسِهِمْ أعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾. "دَرَجَةً" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification); the meaning is: "greater than others in rank." ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفائِزُونَ﴾ — "اَلْفائِزُ" is the one who attains the good he hoped for.

zajjaj:21-21.t: ﴿يُبَشِّرُهم رَبُّهم بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنهُ﴾, that is: He informs them in this world of what awaits them in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His words: ﴿لَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ في مَواطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ ويَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ إذْ أعْجَبَتْكم كَثْرَتُكُمْ﴾, that is: and at Ḥunayn — that is: and He helped you on the day of Ḥunayn. "حُنَيْنٌ" is the name of a valley between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.
His words: ﴿فِي مَواطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ﴾, that is: in places, like your saying "in stations." You say "اِسْتَوْطَنَ فُلانٌ بِالمَكانِ" when he has settled in it. Some grammarians claimed that "مَواطِنَ" is not declined as a triptote here because it is a plural and because it cannot be pluralised. Abū Isḥāq said: It is only "not pluralised" because the alif and tāʾ are not attached to it: we do not say "مَواطِناتٌ" or "حَدائِداتٌ" except in poetry. What was heard of al-Khalīl's view is only that it is a plural not on the pattern of the singular. Its interpretation according to al-Khalīl is that the plurals always end at it, so there is no plural after it: if you made a broken plural of "أقْوالٌ" — that is, pluralised it with a broken plural — and said "أقاوِيلُ", it would not be possible for you to make a broken plural of "أقاوِيلُ"; but you may sometimes say "أقاوِيلاتٌ". The poet said:
فَهُنَّ يَعْلِكْنَ حَدائِداتِها
(So they champ at their iron bits.)
«[Translator's note: the preceding passage is somewhat disordered in the transmitted text and is translated as it stands.]»
According to al-Khalīl, "مَواطِنُ" is not declined as a triptote only because it is a plural and is not on the pattern of the singular. The meaning of "not on the pattern of the singular" is that there is nothing among the forms of singular nouns that comes on its pattern, and that it cannot be pluralised as a singular is pluralised with a broken plural.
The meaning of the verse is that Allah — Majestic and Mighty — made known to them that it is not by their great numbers that they prevail, and that they prevail only by Allah's helping them. So He — Majestic and Mighty — said: ﴿وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ إذْ أعْجَبَتْكم كَثْرَتُكم فَلَمْ تُغْنِ عَنْكم شَيْئًا﴾. It is related that they were twelve thousand on that day; some said they were ten thousand. They were pleased with their great numbers, so Allah made their punishment for being pleased with their numbers, and for their saying "We will not be overcome today for lack of numbers," that He struck them with terror until they turned back in flight, and none remained with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb «[Translator's note: so in the text; the reports usually name Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.]». Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon them until they returned and were victorious; and on that day Allah showed them of His signs that which increased them in clear evidence of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ.
His words: ﴿إنَّما يَعْمُرُ مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 18] — it has also been read "مَسْجِدَ اللَّهِ". Whoever reads "مَسْجِدَ اللَّهِ" means by it the Sacred Mosque, with others included along with it, as you say: "How easy it is for so-and-so to spend the dirham and the dinar!", that is: spending this kind is easy for him. It is also possible that by "مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ" the Sacred Mosque is meant, as you say, when a man rides a horse: "So-and-so has taken to riding horses." Nouns that express genera run on this basis.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His words: ﴿إنَّما المُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ فَلا يَقْرَبُوا المَسْجِدَ الحَرامَ بَعْدَ عامِهِمْ هَذا﴾ — "نَجَسٌ" is said of everything regarded as filthy; and when you mention "اَلرِّجْسَ" you say: "هو رِجْسٌ نَجِسٌ". This took place in the year nine of the Hijra: the Muslims were commanded to prevent the idolaters from the Ḥajj and to kill them wherever they came upon them. ﴿وَإنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً فَسَوْفَ يُغْنِيكُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ إنْ شاءَ﴾ — the people of Mecca had a source of earnings and benefit from those of the idolaters who used to perform the pilgrimage, so Allah made known to them that He would compensate them for that. "اَلْعَيْلَةُ" is poverty. The poet said:
وَما يَدْرِي الفَقِيرُ مَتى غِناهُ ∗∗∗ وما يَدْرِي الغَنِيُّ مَتى يَعِيلُ
(The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, and the rich man does not know when he will become poor.)

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His words — Majestic and Mighty —: ﴿قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ ولا بِاليَوْمِ الآخِرِ ولا يُحَرِّمُونَ ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ﴾ — its meaning is: those who do not believe in Allah with the faith of those who affirm His oneness; for they acknowledged that Allah is their Creator, and that He has a son, and the idolaters associated idols with Him. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic — made known that this is not faith in Allah, and that their belief in the resurrection is not of the kind of our belief, because they do not acknowledge that the people of Paradise eat and drink; so they do not acknowledge the Last Day as Allah — Majestic and Mighty — has made it known, and they do not follow the religion of truth. So Allah commanded the killing of the disbelievers all together, unless they give the jizya out of hand; and accepting the jizya was made obligatory from the People of the Book, namely the Christians and the Jews.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laid down as a sunna regarding the Magians and the Sabians that they be treated like the People of the Book in the acceptance of the jizya. As for the idol-worshippers among the Arabs, for them there is nothing but killing, and likewise for others besides them.
His words: ﴿حَتّى يُعْطُوا الجِزْيَةَ عَنْ يَدٍ وهم صاغِرُونَ﴾ — it was said that the meaning of "عَنْ يَدٍ" is: out of abasement. It was said: "عَنْ يَدٍ" means out of subjugation and abasement, as you say: "اَلْيَدُ في هَذا لِفُلانٍ" (the hand in this belongs to so-and-so), that is: the effective command belongs to so-and-so. And it was said: "عَنْ يَدٍ", that is: as a favour bestowed on them thereby, because accepting the jizya from them and leaving them alive is a favour to them and an abundant act (yad) of kindness.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His words: ﴿وَقالَتِ اليَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ اللَّهِ وقالَتِ النَّصارى المَسِيحُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ﴾ — "عُزَيْرُ" has been read with tanwīn and without tanwīn. The proper way is to keep the tanwīn, because "اِبْنُ" is the khabar (predicate); the tanwīn is dropped only with the adjective, as in your saying "جاءَنِي زَيْدُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو" (Zayd son of ʿAmr came to me): the tanwīn is dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, because "اِبْنُ" is in genitive construct with a proper name, and because the adjective and the thing qualified are like a single thing. But when it is a khabar, then the tanwīn is kept. Dropping the tanwīn is sometimes permissible — weakly — because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; it has been read "قُلْ هو اللَّهُ أحَدُ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ" with the tanwīn dropped because of its being vowelless together with the vowellessness of the bāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the text; the vowelless letter following is the lām of اللَّه here, and the bāʾ of ابن in the case of عُزَيْرُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ.]» in His words "عُزَيْرُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ". There is another way in it: that the khabar is omitted, so that its meaning is: "Uzayr son of Allah is the one we worship," in which case "اِبْنُ" is a naʿt (adjective). There is no disagreement among the grammarians that keeping the tanwīn is better.
His words: ﴿ذَلِكَ قَوْلُهم بِأفْواهِهِمْ﴾ — if someone says: every saying is with the mouth, so what is the benefit of His saying "with their mouths"? The benefit in it is great and clear: the meaning is that there is no clear proof or demonstration in it; it is only a saying with the mouth, with no sound meaning beneath it, because they acknowledge that Allah has not taken a consort, so how can they claim a son for Him? It is only lying and mere talk.
